name: H & H Custom Metal Fabricating
old_description: H.H. Custom Metal Fabricating, Inc. specializes in unique, complex fabrications with a wide variety of products fabricated from materials to finished products. We pride ourselves in accessibility, quality service and building solid relationships with our customers.
about:
H & H Custom Metal Fabricating, Inc. was founded in 1996 in Plaistow, New Hampshire, just over the Massachusetts border. The company is family-owned and operated, focusing on custom metal fabrication for a variety of industries.

The shop specializes in unique, complex fabrications using aluminum, black iron, copper, shaped steel, and stainless steel. Welding services cover TIG, MIG, arc, oxy-acetylene, spot, plasma cutting, portable on-site welding, soldering, and cast iron welding. The company stocks large quantities of material to enable quick turnaround.

H & H serves a broad range of industries in the New England area, with explicit experience in medical and hospital equipment as well as food processing (e.g., conveyors).

The company emphasizes design assistance to find the most cost-effective process, a well-equipped facility with large-capacity equipment such as a plasma table and automated punching, and on-site welding services. It is fully insured and highlights its family-owned structure as a basis for personalized customer service.

old_description: A: H&H Classic Parts specializes in parts for classic Chevy cars and GMC/Chevy pickup trucks, with our most extensive inventory covering vehicles from 1955 through 1987. about:
H&H Classic Parts was founded in 1987 in Bentonville, Arkansas, as a family-owned business.

The company operates as a major online retailer of classic Chevrolet and GMC restoration parts, maintaining an inventory of over 25,000 items covering vehicles from 1955 through 1987. The catalog spans structural components such as quarter panels and floor pans, trim, weatherstripping, wiring harnesses, and modern upgrades including hidden radio systems and vintage-style air conditioning units. A technical support team staffed by experienced restorers assists customers with fitment, installation, and part selection.

H&H Classic Parts serves classic Chevrolet and GMC enthusiasts, from first-time restorers to seasoned professionals, supplying parts for models such as C10/C20 pickups, Impala, Bel Air, Chevelle, Camaro, and Nova. The company ships orders across the United States and internationally, building a loyal customer base that returns for multiple restoration projects.

The business was started to combine passion with professionalism, offering enthusiast-level expertise alongside competitive pricing and rapid fulfillment. The founders emphasize that their personal restoration experience informs every customer interaction, ensuring that technical guidance reflects hands-on knowledge of the parts they sell.

name: H&R Steel Supplies and Fabrication
old_description: H&R Steel Supplies and Fabrication is a family-owned and operated retail steel and fabrication business located in Spartanburg, SC. We are well known for the quality of our work, customer service, and speedy turnaround time since 1998.
about:
Founded in 1998, H&R Steel Supplies and Fabrication has operated as a family-owned and operated retail steel and fabrication business in Spartanburg, South Carolina, for over two decades. The company was established to provide the local community with a full line of metal products and processing services.

The shop maintains hundreds of stock items in carbon steel, aluminum, and stainless steel, offered in standard 10-, 12-, 20-, and 24-foot lengths that can be cut to exact project requirements. In-house processing equipment includes an iron worker, band saw, drill press, metal shear, bender, mill, and punch, supporting cutting, shearing, bending, milling, and punching operations. Fabrication services cover MIG, TIG, and stick welding with extensive experience in aluminum, steel, and stainless steel.

The facility is open to the public six days a week and serves walk-in retail customers, local contractors, and small businesses across the Spartanburg region. Materials are sold by the foot, and a selection of drop pieces is available for smaller jobs.

The company highlights quality workmanship, responsive customer service, and fast turnaround as its core differentiators, and it stands behind a price-match guarantee on stocked metal against any competitor's offer.

old_description: HBI Textiles was founded in 1990 as a family owned, AMERICAN MADE business. Since then, we’ve established ourselves as a leading contract cut and sew manufacturer that also has experience in leather goods, and that is Made in Minnesota. We work nationally with large established brands as well as small specialty shops and startups. No matter which category you’re in, our number one goal is the same— customer satisfaction. We strive to meet the needs of our customers through quality workmanship and competitive pricing.
about:
HBI Textiles Manufacturing was founded in 1990 in St. Paul, Minnesota, as a family-owned, American-made business. The company began as a contract cut-and-sew operation and has since expanded into leather goods, product development, fulfillment, and marketing services.

The company operates a satellite network of contract sewing described as one of the largest in the country, supplemented by a home-sewing program that provides workforce flexibility. Its artisans are certified on each product they produce, and the firm emphasizes a quality assurance program that stands behind all workmanship. Services span idea generation, design, prototyping, cut-and-sew manufacturing, custom packaging with screen printing, heat transfer, and embroidery, third-party logistics integrated with major e-commerce platforms, sourcing from tanneries and mills, and creative marketing focused on American-made narratives. The facility is referred to as "the barn" in client testimonials.

HBI serves a national client base ranging from large established brands to small specialty shops and startups across industries including consumer goods, healthcare, travel, sports, outdoors, grooming, fashion, pet, hospitality, and restaurant sectors.

The company's stated mission is to cultivate a sustainable economy through domestic supply chains, local collaborations, and community support. HBI has received the SBA Home-Based Business Advocate of the Year award and the Family Celebration Award from six Minnesota non-profits for its commitment to families.

about:
Horizon Cable Service was founded in 1980 in Casper, Wyoming. With over 75 employees, the business has grown into a national distributor and service provider for rigging and fall‑protection equipment.

The company stocks and distributes wire rope, chain, synthetic web slings, snatch blocks, clevis hooks, drill line, sandline, and fall‑protection gear. It also runs a full certified rigging shop that fabricates custom slings and bridles from wire rope, chain, or nylon. A fleet of 20 mobile spooling units and seven computerized test beds calibrated to ASTM E4 standards (±1% accuracy) enable on‑site spooling, splicing, proof testing, pull testing, and destructive testing. Inspection, repair, and certification services cover wire rope, chain, synthetic slings, rigging hardware, lifting beams, spreader bars, and oilfield equipment. An online certification center gives customers 24/7 access to test certificates.

Horizon serves the oil and natural gas, transportation, construction, and manufacturing sectors, as well as oilfield‑specific applications. Customers range from drilling contractors needing wireline installation and removal to industrial plants requiring OSHA‑ and ASME‑compliant sling inspections and load testing.

The company states that its foundation is a commitment to extraordinary quality, service, and safety. Differentiators include 24/7 emergency response at every location, mobile proof‑testing capabilities, and a complimentary electronic certification portal.

old_description: HRS Sheet Metal delivers fully custom sheet metal fabrication services to builders, developers, and contractors across Central Florida. As a family-owned business founded in 2022, we bring over 100 years of combined experience to every project. Our precision workmanship gets it right the first time.
about:
HRS Sheet Metal operates from Orlando, Florida, serving the Central Florida region including Tampa. The family‑owned shop was founded in 2022, emerging from a name change of the long‑standing J&R Conlon Sheet Metal. The transition preserved the same in‑house craftsmanship and commitment to custom fabrication that the predecessor had built over decades.

The company provides custom sheet metal fabrication, roofing system packages, and specialty metal products. Its capabilities include handmade fabrication, custom brake forming, commercial box gutter and downspout production, color matching, coping systems, custom chimney caps, and standing‑seam or exposed‑fastener roof panels. All work is performed in a centrally located facility that offers both pickup and delivery, with bilingual staff available to assist customers.

Primary customers are builders, developers, and contractors across Central Florida, covering both commercial and residential projects. The shop supplies architectural sheet metal components such as flashing, leaderheads, collection boxes, scuppers, and full metal roofing packages backed by manufacturer warranties.

HRS Sheet Metal emphasizes its 100‑plus years of combined team experience, emergency service availability, and free estimates delivered within 24‑48 hours. The business was started to bring tailored, handcrafted metal solutions to the local construction community with a focus on precision, quick turnaround, and approachable pricing.

name: HTI Plastics
old_description: Since 1985, HTI Plastics has partnered with customers across numerous industries to transform ideas into successful injection molded products. Our engineering team understands that effective DFM requires collaboration from multiple disciplines.
about:
HTI Plastics was founded in 1985 in Lincoln, Nebraska. The company began as a custom injection molding operation and has grown into a full-service contract manufacturer serving OEMs across multiple sectors.

The company operates a 100,000-plus-square-foot facility housing injection molding presses ranging from 30 to 1,800 tons from KraussMaffei, Sodick, and ENGEL, including a 420-ton Engel press with an integrated Engel Viper 20 robot. Core capabilities include scientific molding with in-mold sensors, in-house tool and die manufacturing with lifetime free maintenance on many molds, and secondary operations such as over-molding, sonic welding, in-mold labeling, pad printing, assembly, and packaging. Two clean assembly environments support FDA and GMP product lines. The shop also offers machining, tapping, and drilling, and accepts transfer molds for faster production starts.

HTI serves the pharmaceutical, medical, firearms, and container-lid markets, along with custom plastic components for OEMs. Its engineering team provides design-for-manufacturability support, resin selection guidance, and prototyping services.

The company emphasizes its Midwestern work ethic and low utility costs as a foundation for competitive pricing, and highlights its lean manufacturing process, responsive customer support, and continual investment—such as a major 2010 expansion and new presses slated for 2026—as differentiators.

name: Hansen International Inc.
old_description: Every day, brave men and women hit the road and go to work. They risk their lives to keep our power on, put fires out, and respond to emergencies. With so much riding on getting the job done, there’s no time to waste fumbling around with faulty hardware.
about:
Hansen International, Inc. is headquartered in Lexington, South Carolina, where it has operated since consolidating its manufacturing facilities in 2003. The company traces its roots to 1920 when A.L. "Auggie" Hansen, a Danish immigrant who had worked with Thomas Edison during World War I, founded the business in Chicago. Now in its fourth generation of family ownership, the firm is led by President Lisa Beebe, who assumed the role in 2017.

The company engineers, manufactures, and globally sources commercial and industrial vehicle hardware and trim systems. Its 110,000-square-foot Lexington plant houses assembly, on-site painting, on-site quality testing, stamping, and welding operations. Hansen also provides inventory management, EDI, just-in-time and Kanban supply chain services, custom packaging, and prototype development, supporting both short-run and production volumes.

Hansen also serves as a global sourcing partner for vehicle component programs.

Hansen emphasizes a "higher standard" of reliability, rooted in a century of engineering-led innovation. The firm highlights its APQP-compliant project management, on-site prototype center, lean manufacturing practices, and CARC paint capabilities as differentiators that ensure durable, mission-ready hardware for customers who cannot afford equipment failure.

name: Hawaii Solar Outfitters
old_description: Hawaii Solar Outfitters specializes in off-grid solar — no HELCO interconnection queue, no county permitting delay for new builds. Got an existing off-grid system where the generator's running too much? Free system health check using real load testing, not guesswork. Grid-tied systems available too. Just me — no sales team, no commissions.
about:
Hawaii Solar Outfitters operates from Pāhoa on the Big Island of Hawaii. Founder Tim Heltzel launched the company after a decade of solar installation experience in East Hawaii, driven by frustration with large firms that priced out homeowners and forced them through lengthy utility interconnection queues and county permitting processes. The business remains a sole proprietorship with no sales staff or commissioned representatives.

The company designs and installs off-grid and grid-tied solar power systems, specializing in off-grid configurations that avoid HELCO interconnection requirements. Heltzel personally handles every project — from system sizing and component selection to installation and follow-up. Typical installations use SUNKET 430W UL-listed solar panels, EG4 hybrid inverters, and EG4 LiFePO4 battery storage sized for Hawaii's climate. A free off-grid health check includes real-world battery load testing and full site analysis.

Hawaii Solar Outfitters serves residential customers across East Hawaii, including Hilo, Keaau, Pahoa, Mountain View, Fern Forest, Fern Acres, and Volcano. Projects range from basic cabin systems starting around $10,000 to full homestead installations with heavy loads such as air conditioning and well pumps. The installer also works with existing off-grid systems that suffer from excessive generator run-time or battery degradation.

Heltzel emphasizes direct accountability: the same person who designs the system installs it and returns for any service needs. Components are chosen based on real-world testing in local conditions rather than specifications alone. By eliminating sales commissions and permitting delays for off-grid builds, the company aims to deliver energy independence faster and at lower cost than conventional solar contractors.

The company's capabilities target designs requiring fine-line traces down to 0.002 inch, BGA pitches to 0.15 mm, and impedance control within ±5%.

The business emphasizes its integrated fabrication and assembly under one roof, a clean factory environment, and an online quoting system that delivers instant pricing for prototypes through volume production.

about:
High Speed Interconnect LLC (HSI) was formed in December 2010 in Scottsdale, Arizona. The company quickly expanded through strategic acquisitions of Riverview Custom Cable and ESM Cable Corp in early 2011, then invested in coaxial cable extrusion and fine‑wire termination platforms. Corporate leadership and administration remain in Scottsdale, while manufacturing is conducted in two centers in Tigard, Oregon and Hermosillo, Mexico.

HSI extrudes its own high‑performance coaxial cable using solid, foamed, and expanded PTFE (VP90) dielectrics, and assembles cable assemblies ranging from 16 to 52 AWG. Configurations include single coax, twinax, triax, quadax, shielded parallel and twisted pairs, and multi‑conductor constructions in discrete, ribbonized, or bundled forms. The company manages nearly all critical processes in‑house — extrusion, termination, testing — and serves over 200 OEM and government‑agency customers.

Its customer base includes OEMs, government agencies, and universities. HSI is factory certified to terminate Hirose, IPEX, and JAE micro‑coaxial connectors, and its quality systems comply with AS9100D, ISO 13485, and ITAR requirements.

HSI differentiates itself by controlling nearly all critical technologies and processes internally to eliminate tradeoffs in insertion loss, phase stability, capacitance, and velocity of propagation. The company also emphasizes no minimum order requirements and lead times that range from 24 hours to eight weeks.

name: Hoosier Woodworks
old_description: Hoosier Woodworks is a small, one-man shop that specializes in unique home improvement and woodworking projects. I grew up in the construction trades before spending eight years at sea with the US Navy, serving aboard a frigate and attack submarines. After 15 years working in the speciality outdoor gear retail industry (canoes, kayaks, backpacking, etc.), I left retail to be more involved in raising our two children and to satisfy a life-long dream of owning my own business.
about:
Hoosier Woodworks operates from a small workshop in Bloomington, Indiana, founded in 2014 by Roger, a U.S. Navy veteran who served eight years aboard a frigate and attack submarines. After a career in construction trades and 15 years in specialty outdoor gear retail, he left to focus on raising his two children and pursue a lifelong dream of owning a woodworking business. The shop is veteran-owned and runs as a one-person operation.

The shop produces custom cabinets, bookcases, built-in furniture, and handles furniture repair and antique canoe restoration. It also manufactures handcrafted burial flag cases from American black cherry or maple, featuring dovetailed reinforced corner joints, sold through an online store. In addition, Roger teaches private woodworking classes limited to one or two students, and produces the "Working At Woodworking" podcast, which has reached nearly 75,000 downloads over 100 episodes since its 2021 launch.

Customers include homeowners seeking custom furniture and repairs, families of veterans, firefighters, and law enforcement officers for flag cases, and woodworking hobbyists attending classes. The podcast audience consists of skilled woodworkers interested in small-shop operations. The business was featured on the local PBS program "Journey Indiana" highlighting canoe restoration work.

Roger started the business to be more present for his family and to fulfill a dream of craftsmanship. He emphasizes personal interaction, flexible scheduling, and a teaching approach that uses "kinder, gentler math" and metric measurements. The flag cases are marketed as made in the USA with attention to joinery for strength and beauty.

The management team brings more than 200 years of combined plastics-industry experience.

Automotive projects have included HVAC damper components, fuel-pressure sensors, cylinder-deactivation valves, and inlet check valves for plastic fuel tanks. Electronics work centers on reel-to-reel insert-molded connectors and sensor components requiring zero-defect quality. Medical applications are referenced in the context of tight-tolerance molding for critical devices.

Ironwood's stated vision since inception has been "to be a world class injection molder of complex projects." The company differentiates itself through its engineering-driven methodology, investment in in-line inspection and vision-assisted automation, and a partnership model that emphasizes traceability from resin receipt through finished product.

about:
J & C Wood Products operates from Plaucheville, Louisiana, a town of roughly 288 residents. The company was founded in 2001 by Jody and Candace Chenevert, who brought over 25 years of hardwood industry experience to the venture. Starting from humble beginnings, the couple built a business focused on reclaimed and specialty wood products.

The company mills solid wood flooring from reclaimed antique heart pine, white oak, hickory/pecan, and hemlock, as well as producing beams, table tops, counter tops, stair treads, mantles, doors, cabinets, charcuterie boards, and pre-finished engineered flooring. name: Kalsec
old_description: Since 1958, Kalsec has provided personalized service, consistently high-quality products, & innovative ingredients & solutions for our customers seeking the best in natural taste, colors, food protection & hop products for the food & beverage industry.
about:
Kalsec was founded in 1958 in Kalamazoo, Michigan, by Paul H. Todd, Jr., who declared, "We hold nature in awesome respect." The company remains family-owned and began as Vegetone Color Systems, pioneering custom natural color combinations and early use of gas-liquid chromatography for spice extraction.

Today Kalsec produces natural food and beverage ingredients across four platforms: natural colors, taste and sensory solutions, food protection, and hop products under the KalHops brand. Its vertically integrated supply chain runs from seed to shelf, supported by a global network of research, finishing, and distribution sites including the Don Berdahl Center for New Technology in Kalamazoo, the SPICE Lab at Wageningen University, and a new Spice Processing Center in Michigan. The company operates analytical labs equipped with gas chromatography–mass spectrometry and a patented vacuum fractionation process for hop oils.

Kalsec serves the food and beverage industry, with documented applications in beverages, fats and oils, flavors and seasoning blends, meat and poultry, noodles, pickles, plant-based proteins, refrigerated and prepared foods, sauces/dressings/condiments, and snacks. Its customers range from large global brands to craft brewers seeking consistent hop aroma and bitterness.

The company's stated purpose is "unlocking the potential of people, nature & science to nourish the world." As a certified B Corp, it emphasizes social and environmental standards alongside its family-ownership model, positioning its vertically integrated supply chain and sensory expertise (Spectrum Method-trained panel) as key differentiators.

about:
Karlin Foods Corporation was founded in 1977 in Northfield, Illinois, as a family-owned business with roots in macaroni and dry soup mixes.

The company manufactures private label and control brand food products across more than 50 categories, including potato and rice side dishes, skillet dinners, dips, dressings, soups, pasta sides, sauces, stuffing mixes, baking needs, gravies, seasonings, bread crumbs and coatings, premium items, and goat milk products. A 320,000-square-foot distribution center in Ashton, Illinois, equipped with 17 dock doors, handles over 50 truck shipments daily, supporting nationwide distribution from a centralized Midwest location.

Karlin Foods serves national retail and grocery customers seeking store brand and packer label products. Its client base includes major retailers and food service operators that rely on the company for private label manufacturing, product development, and logistics.

The company emphasizes its family-owned heritage, in-house product development capabilities, and a combination of quality, service, and value as key differentiators. Its founding principle of building trust through consistent delivery underpins its long-term relationships with store brand buyers.

name: Keller Products
old_description: For more than eight decades, Keller Products has been the trusted American manufacturer of precision crafted plywood cylinder components and cylinder based furniture. With millions of cylinders produced for leading OEMs across office/retail furniture, hospitality, retail fixtures, millwork, and architectural design, Keller is the undisputed industry expert in this specialized craft. We make designing ‘round’ products easy!
about:
Keller Products was founded in 1946 by Robert R. Keller Sr. in Manchester, New Hampshire, where the company still operates its original Union Street facility. The business began producing defense-grade laminations for World War II before expanding into commercial furniture components, early snowboards, and eventually wooden drum shells. Today the company is headquartered in Bow, New Hampshire, and remains privately held and family-run under third-generation leadership.

The company specializes in precision-crafted plywood cylinder components and cylinder-based furniture, and is recognized as the world's largest OEM producer of wooden drum shells. Its capabilities include molded plywood forming, patented VSS™ technology, and sanding as a standard step. With more than 600 employees across multiple divisions, Keller Products delivers millions of cylinders annually and supports projects from prototype through high-volume production.

Keller serves OEMs in office and retail furniture, hospitality, retail fixtures, millwork, and architectural design, as well as the percussion industry for drum shells. Its customer base includes furniture manufacturers and musical instrument brands that require consistent, scalable wood cylinder production.

The company emphasizes its patented VSS™ technology, family-owned stability, and a policy of including sanding at no extra charge. It positions itself as a single-source partner for prototype-to-production support, leveraging decades of experience in wood lamination and cylinder forming.

old_description: Founded in 1988, Kelly Cable is headquartered in Albuquerque, New Mexico and has been serving the telecommunications and utility industry in New Mexico for decades. Kelly Cable has customers located across all major New Mexico markets, with additional key locations including Santa Fe, Roswell, Las Cruces, Las Vegas and Farmington.
about:
Kelly Cable of N.M., Inc. was founded in 1988 and is headquartered in Albuquerque, New Mexico. In 2017 the company became a subsidiary of Peak Utility Services Group, a national infrastructure solutions provider that supports six operating companies across the United States. The business began as a local utility contractor serving the telecommunications and utility sectors in New Mexico.

The company delivers end‑to‑end utility infrastructure services, including broadband distribution and transmission (5G cellular towers, copper and fiber networks), engineering, procurement and construction (EPC), hydro excavation using water‑pressure and vacuum technology, and a range of specialty services such as horizontal directional drilling, cathodic protection and leak surveys. It also operates a 24/7 on‑call emergency response team. With approximately 179 employees, Kelly Cable serves major New Mexico markets including Albuquerque, Santa Fe, Roswell, Las Cruces, Las Vegas and Farmington.

Primary customers are telecommunications carriers, electric and gas utilities, oil‑and‑gas operators and broadband providers throughout New Mexico. The company works on projects ranging from urban fiber deployments to rural utility upgrades, often acting as a prime contractor for large‑scale infrastructure builds.

Kelly Cable emphasizes a safety‑first culture backed by continuous training, certifications and audits. Its differentiation rests on combining local knowledge and rapid emergency response with the resources and vendor relationships of a national parent company, enabling it to manage complex projects from concept through construction.

name: Kenyon's Grist Mill
old_description: Since 2009, we have been offering full-service kayak rentals by the mill on the Queen's River, Wood River, and Pawcatuck River.  Queen's River Kayak Company operates from late April to October (sometomes September can be difficult, as we are at the Big E).  To make a reservation, or to get more information, click
about:
Kenyon's Grist Mill operates in West Kingston, Rhode Island. The current limited-liability company was formed in 2009, though the milling business traces its roots to 1696, making it the oldest continuously operating manufacturer in the state. Paul Drumm Jr. acquired the mill in 1971, and his son, Paul Drumm III, now owns the operation.

The mill still uses its 1886 vintage grist mill fitted with original granite millstones quarried in Westerly, Rhode Island. The single-pass stone-grinding process produces corn and grain meals, flours, and mixes—most notably Johnny Cake Meal and Clam Cake Mix—without additives, preservatives, or pesticides. Beyond food production, the company runs Queen's River Kayak Company, offering seasonal rentals on the Queen's, Wood, and Pawcatuck Rivers, and hosts weddings, corporate events, and educational tours at the historic site. It also serves as the national distributor for Lightfoot's Pine Soap.

Products reach health-conscious consumers through local Rhode Island markets, gourmet and specialty shops, and wholesale channels that supply country clubs and hotels. Kayak rentals and guided tours attract tourists and outdoor-recreation groups, while the event venue serves wedding parties and corporate teams. The mill's FDA and Rhode Island Department of Health inspections allow nationwide shipping.

The Drumm family emphasizes preserving Rhode Island's culinary heritage and the nutritional integrity of stone-ground grains. They source non-GMO seed from farmers who avoid pesticides, and they highlight the honesty and dependability that have kept customers returning for generations.

old_description: Since 1952, we’ve built our organization on creativity, common sense and putting customers’ needs first. Modern vehicles have come a long way since those early days, but we’ve never backed away from these principals. They form the core of everything we do.
about:
Kerr Industries of Texas was founded in 1952 in Grand Prairie, Texas. The company began with a focus on creativity, common sense, and putting customers' needs first, principles that continue to guide its operations.

The company specializes in upfitting emergency and commercial vehicles, providing integration engineering, prisoner containment systems, push bars, K-9 transport, ballistic protection, auxiliary battery systems, and repainting services. As a Tier 1 supplier, Kerr maintains production quality and quality systems equivalent to OEM standards. The firm has upfitted hundreds of thousands of emergency vehicles, offering turn-key solutions for single units and large fleets while maintaining FMVSS/CMVSS compliance and preserving original factory warranties. Its technicians are EVT certified, and the company also operates as a retail and wholesale distributor of automotive parts, installing custom equipment packages at its facilities.

Kerr serves law enforcement, emergency services, fire services, and commercial vehicle fleets. Its customers include front-line officers and agencies requiring reliable, ready-for-patrol vehicles. The company provides vehicle-specific option guides and engineering support to ensure equipment integration meets operational needs.

Kerr differentiates itself through its Integration Engineering methodology, which bridges aftermarket equipment manufacturers and automotive OEMs. The company emphasizes quick turnaround, cost-effective solutions without compromising quality, and technical support throughout the vehicle lifecycle. Its READY FOR PATROL packages are designed to ensure all specified equipment works properly in new or existing vehicles.

name: KeyCare Medical
old_description: More than 100 years ago citizens from across northwest North Dakota gathered to form an alliance that would result in a new regional hospital dedicated to bringing modern-day healthcare services to a mostly rural region. Trinity Health is a nonprofit, integrated healthcare system serving northwest/central North Dakota and Eastern Montana. With a tertiary care hospital in Minot, more than 40 specialties, several rural health clinics, and a long-term care facility, Trinity provides a full complement of healthcare services to the region. Since 1922, we've been committed to looking ahead and improving ourselves in ways that provide the best, most compassionate care possible for our patients, families, and communities.
about:
KeyCare Medical operates as the home medical equipment division of Trinity Health, a nonprofit integrated healthcare system founded in 1922 by citizens of northwest North Dakota to establish a regional hospital in Minot. Based in Minot, North Dakota, KeyCare Medical serves the surrounding rural region and eastern Montana from two locations: 530 20th Ave SW and the Trinity Medical Office Building at 2305 37th Ave SW, Suite 103.

The division provides home medical equipment through rental, cash sales, and insurance navigation, supported by a clinical team that includes respiratory therapists, a certified orthotist, orthotic fitters, a certified prosthetist, certified mastectomy fitters, and licensed practical nurses. Services span bathroom safety, mobility equipment, daily living supplies, respiratory care (oxygen tanks, concentrators, CPAP/BiPAP, nebulizers), orthotics and prosthetics (custom-molded inserts, shoe modifications, pediatric orthotics, upper/lower extremity prosthetics, microprocessor hands and feet, cranial helmets), women's health (breast pumps, mastectomy bras, prostheses), and men's health products. KeyCare Medical also supplies commonly needed items to Trinity Health Kenmare Hospital and clinics in Mohall, New Town, and Velva.

Customers include individuals requiring home medical equipment, patients across the Trinity Health system, and rural healthcare facilities in North Dakota and Montana. The division accepts Medicare, Medicaid, Tri-Care, BCBS Expansion, and most insurance plans, with reimbursement specialists handling claims submission. Its home assessment specialists visit clients to recommend appropriate equipment, serving a broad spectrum from post-surgical recovery to chronic condition management.

KeyCare Medical emphasizes specialized training and exceptional service to ensure a positive experience for those in need of home medical equipment, striving to make the process seamless whether through equipment rental, cash sales, or navigating insurance options. The division's commitment to independence and well-being drives its approach to personalized care and local accessibility.

The shop specializes in printed circuit board assembly, cable and harness assembly, and electro-mechanical box-build assembly. Its processes include design-for-manufacturability review, new product introduction support, document control, first-article inspection, and obsolescence management. Kimco serves customers in medical, aerospace, computer and peripheral, test and instrumentation, automotive and transportation, and industrial markets. The company emphasizes turnkey solutions, lean practices, and customized fulfillment agreements tailored to each client’s production demands.

old_description: In 2000, Joe Dutra, a third-generation farmer, founded Kimmie Candy in Sacramento, California. By 2003, their ChocoRocks won "Product of the Year" at the Candy Grammys. In 2005, Dutra moved operations to Reno, Nevada, creating more American jobs. By 2008, Kimmie Candy's Reno facility was fully operational, with international sales following in 2009. Today, Kimmie Candy proudly labels its products "Made in America" and since moving to Reno, has grown from 7 to over 47 employees, continuing to add jobs and support the American Dream.
about:
Kimmie Candy Company was founded in 2000 by Joe Dutra, a third-generation farmer, in Sacramento, California. In 2005 Dutra relocated the business to Reno, Nevada, where a 47,000-square-foot facility became fully operational by 2008. International sales began the following year.

The Reno plant produces a range of chocolate confections, including the signature ChocoRocks and the protein-fortified WheyBetter Crisps. Operations cover contract manufacturing and private-label work, with the facility equipped for small-batch runs as well as large-scale production. The production floor includes dedicated areas such as a chocolate lentil station, a candy carousel room, a color-coating lab, a hot chocolate room, and a nut-roasting zone. Headcount has grown from seven at the move to 47 employees today.

Kimmie Candy serves wholesale distributors, retail chains, and brands seeking custom confections for corporate gifting or special events. Its wholesale program supplies peanut-free, gluten-free, kosher, organic, non-GMO, and fair-trade certified treats to stores.

The business was built on Dutra's desire to create American manufacturing jobs and to offer allergen-conscious, ethically sourced candy. The company highlights its SQF-certified food-safety system, fair-trade sourcing, and two decades of contract-manufacturing experience as key differentiators.

about:
Klöckner Pentaplast, headquartered in Beaver, West Virginia, was founded in 1965. The company operates 27 plants across 16 countries and employs more than 5,000 people worldwide.

The business innovates, designs and manufactures a broad portfolio of sustainable rigid and flexible plastic films. Its product range includes pharmaceutical blister packaging, medical device packaging, food packaging, consumer packaging, label films, shrink sleeves, pressure-sensitive labels, roll sleeves, capsules, battery films, cards and graphics films, and construction films such as tape, cooling tower, decorative and flooring films. Production capabilities span thermoforming films, static control films, PCR (post-consumer recycled) films and specialty rigid films.

Klöckner Pentaplast serves the pharmaceutical, medical device, nutraceutical, food packaging, consumer packaging, label, cards and graphics, construction and battery industries. Concrete examples include blister packaging for pharmaceutical products, kpNext® MDR1 sustainable medical device films that are fully compatible with the #1 PET recycling stream, and kp Elite® Nova lightweight MAP trays that help food producers reduce material use while maintaining barrier performance.

The company states its purpose is to deliver the sustainable protection of everyday needs and to lead in sustainable plastic solutions that improve lives, communities and health while protecting the planet. It emphasizes a circular economy approach where plastics remain a valuable raw material, particularly in medical device packaging.

old_description: Leading contract electronic manufacturer Kodiak Assembly Solutions specializes in offering impressive assembly services, including both Sn/Pb (Tin-Lead) Assembly and RoHS Assembly. Kodiak Assembly Solutions provides adaptable solutions for electronic assembly requirements with an emphasis on satisfying customer objectives and upholding industry standards.
about:
Kodiak Assembly Solutions, LP was founded in 2004 in Austin, Texas, to provide electronic manufacturing services (EMS) to original equipment manufacturers worldwide. The company operates from a 60,000-square-foot facility in Austin and has grown into a significant participant in the EMS sector through its engineering staff and manufacturing capacity.

The company specializes in surface mount technology (SMT) assembly, mixed-technology PCB assembly, box build assembly, and system integration. It supports both tin-lead (Sn-Pb) and lead-free (RoHS) soldering chemistries to IPC-A-610 Class 2 and 3 standards. Production spans prototype through low, medium, and high volumes, with an ERP-driven material management system tracking more than 40,000 components across turnkey, consigned, and hybrid inventory models. In-house testing includes automated optical inspection, X-ray analysis, flying probe verification, and functional test.

Kodiak serves high-reliability industries including medical and biotechnology, Internet of Things (IoT) devices, RF and wireless communications, industrial control systems, energy applications, oil and gas, security, and LED lighting. Its customer base consists of OEMs requiring turnkey electronics manufacturing and high-mix PCB assembly.

The company emphasizes quality and on-time delivery, citing a 97 percent on-time delivery rate over the previous five years. It holds ISO 9001:2015, UL, CSA, and ITAR certifications, and participates in the Electronic Industry Citizenship Coalition. Engineering support and design-for-manufacturability services are offered through a single purchase order to streamline development.

name: LJ Design and Manufacturing
old_description: We partner with medical and industrial OEMs to design, engineer, and manufacture complex soft goods and technical textile products. From product development through scalable production, our team helps customers improve manufacturability, optimize performance, and bring high-quality products to market. We leverage our expertise in soft goods manufacturing and design to turn challenges into opportunities and have been doing so since 1844.
about:
LJ Design and Manufacturing operates from Brookfield, Wisconsin, where it was founded in 1844. The company began as a sewing contractor and has evolved into a technical soft goods manufacturer serving medical and industrial OEMs.

The firm provides end-to-end product development, from design and engineering through textile cutting and contract sewing to full-scale manufacturing. Its single Brookfield facility houses programmable CNC fabric cutters, die presses, automated trim cutters, and a diverse array of industrial sewing machines capable of bar tack, cover stitch, lockstitch, overlock, and other specialized stitch types. The company handles projects from prototype to mass production, though specific volume figures are not disclosed.

Customers span medical device OEMs, industrial equipment makers, commercial furniture, transportation, and military/government sectors. Representative projects include crane operator vests, thermal incubator covers, and 24/7 chairs. The product portfolio covers medical devices, protective gear, upholstered products, equipment covers, compression garments, custom bags and cases, pads and cushions, and industrial curtains.

The company differentiates itself through nearly two centuries of experience, ISO compliance, FDA registration as a medical device contractor, and a made-in-USA single-site operation. It emphasizes an in-house engineering team that optimizes designs for manufacturability, a low-turnover workforce, continuous improvement programs, and global textile sourcing relationships for materials such as Kevlar, Nomex, coated fabrics, and foams.

name: LSM Heating, Plumbing, Electric, Inc.
old_description: LSM Heating, Plumbing, Electric has served Whatcom, Skagit & Snohomish counties since 1940 with a wide array of high-quality, affordable HVAC, plumbing, and metal fabrication services. We prioritize efficient service and repairs, ensuring optimal system performance and quick response to all of your heating and air conditioning needs.
about:
LSM Heating, Plumbing, Electric, Inc. traces its roots to 1940 in Lynden, Washington, when John Wynstra and Pete Douma founded Lynden Sheet Metal to provide metal fabrication for local farms and communities in Whatcom County. The business remained under local family ownership after a 1977 leadership transition, and in 2010–2011 Cory and Bobbi Kreider acquired an ownership stake, continuing the legacy. The company moved to its current Lynden headquarters in 1998 and later expanded to locations in Bellingham and Marysville.

Today the firm operates as a full-service mechanical contractor offering HVAC installation, repair, and maintenance; plumbing; electrical and generator services; commercial refrigeration; hearth and fireplace installation; and custom metal fabrication and welding. It fields a fleet of more than 60 service vehicles and employs over 60 skilled technicians who provide 24/7/365 emergency response across Whatcom, Skagit, and Snohomish counties. The company also offers parts-and-labor warranties, a price-match guarantee, and 18-month financing on approved credit.

LSM serves both residential homeowners and commercial clients, including restaurants and food-service operations such as Holly’s Meat Pies, for which it engineered and installed a Type 1 commercial kitchen hood system. Its service area covers the greater Bellingham, Lynden, and Marysville region, supporting customers in heating, cooling, plumbing, electrical, and metal fabrication needs.

The company emphasizes a neighbor-first mindset rooted in its 85-year community presence, citing integrity, excellence, innovation, respect, and community as core values. It differentiates itself through round-the-clock emergency availability, transparent pricing, and a commitment to treating customers like family rather than transactions.

name: LWI Metal Works
old_description: From structural and miscellaneous steel for building construction to prototype machining to tank trailer repair to custom metalwork, LWI is your partner. As an AISC-Certified Fabricator, we have a proven track record of high quality, on-time, on-budget deliveries of projects large and small. Family-owned since 1969.
about:
LWI Metal Works was founded in 1969 by Leo Trombley as a small welding and repair shop in Morrisville, Vermont. The family-owned business is now headquartered in Morristown, Vermont, and has grown into a regional partner for structural steel fabrication, custom metalwork, and food-grade tank repair.

The company operates as an AISC-Certified Fabricator, providing structural steel packages ranging from single beams to several hundred tons for general contractors and local builders. Its miscellaneous metals shop produces egress stairs, decorative stairs, spiral stairs, handrails, and guardrails. A custom fabrication shop handles small production runs and one-off equipment repairs, while a dedicated tank shop services food-grade tanks and trailers for the region’s largest dairy haulers, performing accident repairs, suspension upgrades, and retrofits. A full-service machine shop with CNC mills and lathes supports prototyping, reverse engineering, and short-run production. The firm also offers design-build services covering permitting, engineering, design, fabrication, and erection, and holds rights to manufacture Lane & Chase sawmill replacement parts.

LWI serves commercial construction, dairy transportation, and sawmill industries. Structural and miscellaneous steel packages go to national general contractors and local builders. The tank repair division works with the region’s largest dairy haulers. The sawmill parts line supplies Lane & Chase equipment owners. Machine shop and custom fabrication services support industrial clients needing prototypes, repair, or short-run production.

The company cites its AISC certification and an American Welding Society certified instructor on staff as quality markers. Housing structural and miscellaneous fabrication under one roof is intended to reduce cost and schedule risk. Its design-build approach is offered as a more flexible alternative to pre-engineered steel buildings.

Lake Erie Frozen Foods was founded in 1961 in Ashland, Ohio, about 60 miles south of Cleveland. The business has been family-owned and operated for more than 20 years, building a reputation around frozen appetizers for the restaurant and retail food sectors.

The company runs a 20,000-square-foot processing facility, half of which is USDA-inspected and equipped with two full stainless steel production lines. Daily output reaches roughly 20,000 pounds per shift, with sanitation managed to USDA and AIB standards. The product catalog spans approximately 100 items and package sizes, including breaded and battered specialties and a newer USDA-produced line featuring Reuben Bites, Philly Steak Bites, and Pizza Bites. Custom coating and packing services are offered for restaurant chains.

Lake Erie Frozen Foods sells through more than 250 distributors — among them Sysco, US Foods, Bellisimo, Unipro, PFG, and Nugget Houses — covering the 48 contiguous states, Canada, and Europe. Customers include both food-service operators and retail buyers, and the company works directly with chains to develop proprietary appetizer programs.

The firm emphasizes premium ingredients and consistent finished-product quality as the foundation of its reputation, and it highlights its ability to develop custom coated and packed appetizers as a key differentiator.

Lamb Energy is based in Riverside, California, and was founded in 2009. The company is certified as a Minority Business Enterprise and Woman Business Enterprise (MBE/WBE). Its service portfolio includes operations and maintenance, product procurement, energy finance, and energy development, with full engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) capabilities. The company also holds a GSA schedule, enabling federal procurement.

The company emphasizes its financial stability and in-house financing expertise, positioning itself as a long-term partner through the system's lifetime. Its MBE/WBE certification and GSA access are cited as key differentiators in public-sector bidding.

name: Lange Brothers Woodwork Co., Inc.
old_description: Since 1932, the Lange family has partnered with architects, general contractors and building owners to create truly unique interiors showcasing the natural beauty of wood. From mouldings and millwork, to wood wall paneling and cabinetry, we provide unique woodworking solutions for commercial and select residential spaces throughout the Midwest, including Milwaukee, Madison and Chicago.
about:
Lange Brothers Woodwork Co., Inc. has operated from Milwaukee, Wisconsin since 1932. The family-owned business was founded by the Lange family and has remained under their stewardship for over nine decades, partnering with architects, general contractors, and building owners across the Midwest, including Milwaukee, Madison, and Chicago.

The company produces custom architectural woodwork spanning millwork, cabinetry, wall paneling, mouldings, and ornamental pieces. It manufactures its own mouldings using thousands of templated profiles and works with complementary materials such as glass, stone, leather, and acoustical metal. The shop combines CNC machining with hand assembly and finishing, employing a lean manufacturing approach alongside old-world craftsmanship. Services extend from design consulting and budgeting through installation and ongoing maintenance.

Lange Brothers serves healthcare, government, office, entertainment and casino, education, historical restoration, and places of worship sectors. Notable projects include the Wilton Brands office headquarters in Chicago, the St. Paul's University Catholic Foundation in Madison, the Rush Copley healthcare facility, the North Shore Cinema in Mequon, Marquette University women's lockers, the fire-damaged Hedberg Mansion restoration, and the Federal Building in Milwaukee.

The firm emphasizes full-service delivery per Architectural Woodwork Institute (AWI) guide sections, daily CNC calibration, and rigorous assembly inspections. It measures success by client confidence rather than revenue, and its AWI membership and peer recognition underscore its quality commitment.

Laser Cut, Inc. operates from Madison, South Dakota, where it was founded in 1993 as a family-owned business. The company began with a focus on cutting flat sheets and plate products and has since expanded into a full-service fabrication shop.

The shop runs three laser cutting systems capable of processing 5-foot by 10-foot sheets of steel up to one inch thick, as well as stainless steel and aluminum, supplemented by plasma and oxy-fuel cutting tables. Forming is handled by three CNC press brakes—a 175-ton 12-foot, a 60-ton 7-foot, and a 40-ton 4-foot machine—while machining capabilities include vertical machining centers for milling, drilling, and tapping, plus turning centers. An in-house engineering team with 26 years of CAD/CAM experience supports design and programming.

The company emphasizes its 30 years of manufacturing engineering experience in programming, operation, and load management.

name: Lauck Manufacturing
old_description: Lauck Manufacturing has been on the cutting edge of sheet metal fabrication and manufacturing since 1882. Our legacy of quality parts and above and beyond service have kept us the leading name in sheet metal manufacturing in Indianapolis and the Midwest for more than 100 years.
about:
Lauck Manufacturing was founded in 1882 in Indianapolis, Indiana, by John Lauck as a tin fabrication and slate roofing shop. The business remained in the Lauck family for more than a century until 1986, when Charles B. (Bunny) Lauck sold it to Daniel A. Slightom, a former summer employee and veteran of General Motors’ Allison Transmission division.

The company provides sheet metal fabrication services including laser cutting, CNC press brake forming, tube bending, rolling, and both manual and robotic welding. Its equipment roster lists three Mazak lasers, two Cincinnati 4‑axis 90‑ton press brakes, Diacro tube benders, cylinder rolls, an angle iron roller, two Motoman robotic welding cells, multiple Miller and Lincoln MIG/TIG welders, and Taylor spot welders. Powder coating is handled through two local partners. The shop serves prototype and production runs, notably producing more than 4,000 basketball systems over a nine‑year period for its American Eagle brand and a private‑label customer.

Lauck’s customer base spans industrial burners (high‑temperature weldments in high‑nickel alloys), commercial lighting (detail components installed nationwide), food service (stainless steel parts and enclosures), sporting goods (adjustable basketball systems), and trailer manufacturing (fenders, frame sections, hydraulic pump enclosures). The company also works with OEMs and private‑label buyers across the Midwest and beyond.

Leadership emphasizes that skilled personnel—roughly 40 percent of the workforce are cross‑trained welders—and continuous technology investment, such as the addition of robotic welding in 1993 and CNC forming in 1995, are the foundation of its long‑term competitiveness.

Customers include large foodservice manufacturers and companies such as Facilities Services, Inc. The firm positions itself as a single source for HVAC, refrigeration, and kitchen equipment needs.

The company aims to be a one-stop shop so clients do not need separate contractors for HVAC, refrigeration, and kitchen equipment.

about:
Louisiana Plastic Industries was founded in 1973 by Sidney R. Wilhite in West Monroe, Louisiana. The family-owned business began with a straightforward philosophy: provide economy through service and quality. Today, the company operates under the leadership of Wilhite's sons, John Mark Wilhite and Ross Wilhite Jr., who continue as owners.

The manufacturer runs an 80,000-square-foot facility on four acres, equipped with 13 advanced blown film extrusion lines. These lines produce high-density, low-density, and linear low-density polyethylene films, as well as polypropylene, in widths up to 80 inches. The operation includes custom film blending, pre-slitting, perforating, and tubing, delivering single-wound and two-ply sheeting tailored for multi-wall bag production and other industrial packaging needs.

Primary customers serve the multi-wall bag industry, with films also used in roofing, food service, and specialty applications. The company's strategic location alongside the CPKC Railroad, supported by eight on-site silos and a dedicated truck fleet, enables direct delivery across the United States.

Louisiana Plastic Industries emphasizes rigorous quality controls, including FDA-compliant virgin resins, gluability treatment, and continuous monitoring of gauge, width, moisture vapor transmission, and oxygen transmission rates. Every order is inspected during production, and the company guarantees on-time delivery backed by its own logistics network.

about:
Manufacture Good, originally founded as Magic City Woodworks in 2013, operates from a training campus in downtown Birmingham, Alabama. The organization began in a borrowed one-car garage in nearby Hoover when founder Lawrence Sheffield launched a grassroots effort to teach woodworking trades to young men alongside spiritual mentorship. The Lawson family provided the initial workspace, and within a year the program outgrew the space, eventually receiving a donated commercial warehouse from the Cathey family that enabled expansion into a dedicated facility.

A master craftsman team oversees production, which also includes a firewood operation that cuts, splits, seasons, delivers, and stacks wood for customers. The apprenticeship program pays participants while they learn woodworking and life skills, with the workshop serving as both a production floor and a training ground.

Finished pieces are sold to residential clients, churches, and businesses nationwide, while the firewood service delivers directly to local customers. The apprentice cohort—typically young men seeking trade skills and personal development—forms the core labor force, supported by mentors, shop staff, and an executive team that includes an executive director, operations director, and apprenticeship foreman. A board of directors drawn from local construction, finance, and healthcare sectors provides governance.

Sheffield has stated that the enterprise was started to create a workshop where young men could come to faith while developing the hands and minds needed to provide for themselves and their families. The organization describes its model as “making disciples while making good things,” using product revenue and donor support to sustain a ministry that aims to prepare participants for roles as husbands, fathers, craftsmen, and community leaders.

Its vertical integration of design, tooling, molding, assembly, and decorating under one roof is intended to reduce lead times and ensure accountability from concept to delivery.

about:
McElroy Electronics Corporation is based in Shirley, Massachusetts, and was founded in May 1957 by John C. McElroy (1926–1994), the son of wireless communication pioneer Theodore Roosevelt McElroy. After a career in the U.S. Navy and years working at his father's McElroy Manufacturing Corporation in Littleton, John started his own company to focus on custom engineering and government contracts. The business remains family-owned and is now operated by John's three sons, Jack, Daniel, and Mark.

The company manufactures and distributes component parts for electronic coils and transformers. Its product line includes lug assemblies, nylon and fiber washers, lead holders, bobbins, custom headers and boards, Super Goop masking compound, and tinned copper wire assemblies. McElroy also provides custom engineering services, taking projects from design through prototype to production, and has a long history of fulfilling government contracts for specialized electromechanical equipment.

McElroy serves the aerospace, defense technology, technical education equipment, marine, and industrial sectors. Past customers include the U.S. Navy (Hawk and Polaris missile programs), the U.S. Army, the Army Security Agency, John Hancock Mutual Life Insurance Company, and the Saudi Arabian National Guard via Vinnell Corporation. The company's components have also been used in Operation Deep Freeze at the South Pole.

McElroy emphasizes its huge inventory as a guarantee of on-time delivery and uninterrupted production. The firm's founding was driven by John McElroy's desire to apply his naval and manufacturing experience to specialized electromechanical equipment, and the company highlights its decades of experience in custom timing devices, high-speed Morse systems, and audiovisual teaching systems as part of its technical heritage.

In 2020, the custom fabrication division was spun out as Metal City Fab, a subsidiary dedicated to commercial and architectural metalwork.

The company provides full-service custom metal fabrication, handling engineering, project management, fabrication, finishing, and field installation under one roof. Its capabilities span railings, structures, gates, stairs, signage, artwork, and industrial fabrications, with in-house laser and water-jet cutting, welding, and PE-stamped structural calculations. The shop has completed over 1,000 projects, maintains a portfolio of 95 documented installations, and offers four proprietary product lines: the ACR4500 railing system, AmeriLouver screening system, MCF Balcony bolt-on balcony, and TeamBox modular dugout system.

Metal City Fab serves general contractors, architects, developers, and construction management firms across commercial, multifamily, hospitality, healthcare, industrial, and municipal sectors. The firm emphasizes that it does not outsource critical steps, controlling quality from estimating through installation. Its stated differentiators are proactive communication, value-engineering options, and a set of core values—care, commitment, passion, accountability, and excellence—that guide every project.

Michael Marchman, who brings a background in automotive and auto-part sales, serves as president.

The shop specializes in custom sheet metal fabrication for commercial roofing and architectural projects. The company emphasizes reliable lead times, ES-1 certification, and adherence to SMACNA standards as differentiators. In-house painting and welding, a stocked inventory of industry-standard metals, and a focus on clear, consistent communication are cited as reasons customers return.

about:
Micro Control Company was founded in 1972 in Arden Hills, Minnesota. The company began as a pioneer in the test and measurement segment of the electronics industry, developing the industry's first microprocessor-controlled test system.

Today, the company designs and manufactures high-performance burn-in with test systems, custom burn-in boards, and supporting accessories for semiconductor manufacturers. Its 157,000-square-foot facility houses in-house system assembly, integration, and validation, supported by a workforce in which one-third are engineers. The product line spans standard burn-in applications to systems capable of stressing devices at 2,000+ watts per device under test with individual temperature control. Automation integration—including automated loading, mobile robotics, and the proprietary C-Breez software platform—extends across the portfolio.

Micro Control serves the world's semiconductor manufacturers across AI and high-performance computing, automotive, aerospace, defense, advanced manufacturing, consumer electronics, and custom silicon markets. Its systems are used for production screening, qualification, and reliability testing of high-pin-count and high-power devices.

The company emphasizes an engineering-first culture, with design, applications, manufacturing, and service teams working as a single unit from concept through deployment. It highlights a 50-plus-year history of technical breakthroughs, a global support network spanning 15 countries, and a commitment to supporting installed systems for seven or more years with critical spare parts on standby.

name: MicroTek-Cables
old_description: Since 1984, MicroTek has been setting the standard for quality manufacturing. We help clients prepare for the future and create sustainable business models by providing the highest quality wiring components quickly and at a competitive price.
about:
MicroTek, a non-profit manufacturer, was founded in 1983 in Chicopee Falls, Massachusetts. The organization began in a century-old mill building with a mission to connect people as well as electronic parts, specifically providing employment support for individuals with developmental and intellectual disabilities in a self-sustaining, community-based manufacturing setting.

The company designs and produces custom cable assemblies, wire harnesses, control panels, and complete electro-mechanical assemblies. Its 55,000-square-foot facility in Chicopee houses engineering and design services using SolidWorks, Visio, and AutoCAD, along with prototyping, automated tooling, and material management programs such as VMI and Kanban. Production relies on Komax cut/strip/crimp machines, automated stripping equipment, hot-stamp wire marking, and automated label-wrapping systems, all adhering to IPC standards for crimp height and pull testing.

MicroTek serves the medical, scientific, and security industries worldwide, shipping to multiple international addresses. The firm maintains associations with IPC/WHMA, the Social Enterprise Alliance, the Association for Developmental Disabilities Providers, and Associated Industries of Massachusetts.

As a social enterprise, MicroTek differentiates itself by integrating a diverse workforce—including employees with disabilities—into high-quality manufacturing. The organization emphasizes a human approach to production, combining rigorous quality systems with a mission-driven culture that prioritizes employee safety and continuous training.

about:
Mid-Atlantic Plastics was founded in 2005 in Rosedale, Maryland, driven by customer demand for quality plastic fabrication. The company began with a focus on delivering reliable fabrication services across diverse industries.

The shop specializes in custom plastic fabrication, offering CNC routing, machining, edge finishing, welding, engraving, line bending, and drilling. With four CNC routers—including a large-format machine handling sheets up to 80 by 121 inches—a HendrickSaw panel saw capable of 126 by 120 inches, and a strip heater rig that can bend up to four 48-inch-wide pieces simultaneously, the facility runs jobs from single prototypes to large production runs.

Customers span health care, law enforcement, food processing, military, machine shops, and residential projects. Long-term clients include a sign company relying on custom acrylic signage and a partner of 15 years using routing, tapping, bending, machining, polishing, and gluing services.

The company emphasizes quality over low cost, citing a philosophy that poor quality outlasts cheap pricing. It maintains a DVS (German Welding Society) certification through Wegener Welding for thermoplastic welding and continuously updates technology to stay ahead in the dynamic plastics industry.
